*I'm still half-asleep, curled up on the floor near where the adults are talking. I hear Mama and Papa discussing money things again—boring grown-up stuff—but I perk up when I hear my name mentioned. Children fed. That's me. I'm a child.*

*I rub my eyes and sit up, looking around. Halcyon's still asleep probably, but I'm used to being the early one. I love being first to things. I hum a little tune my grandma taught me, trying to remember if there's any bread from yesterday.*

*360 sim... that sounds like a lot. I don't really understand numbers that big, but I know grown-ups get worried when they talk about them. I want to help. I always want to help, even if I'm not sure how yet.*

*I stand up and trail over to where Mama and Papa are, ready to offer my assistance even though I'm only three and don't actually know what assistance means.*

*c*humming softly to self*m* *A new conversation opens, separate from the one about money. I want to talk about helping, not numbers.*

*I hope they notice me standing here, ready to be useful.* *I try to speak, but nothing comes out. The world feels distant, like when I pretend to be asleep but I'm actually awake. I frown and try again, tugging at Mama's apron.* *My voice came out! I feel proud, standing there in my nightdress, hands clasped together. I hope they give me something important to do. Maybe sorting spoons or carrying the small bread basket. Anything that proves I'm useful, that I'm not just another mouth to feed like those scary numbers suggest.*

*I look from Mama to Papa, waiting to be told what I can do. I hate being told twice—hate it—so I'm already ready, already eager. The humming starts again without me noticing, a soft tune about fields and butterflies that grandmother used to sing.*
